title: The Replication Problem
text:
Replication studies have become a central concern in experimental psychology. Researchers attempt to repeat earlier experiments using the same methods to determine whether the original findings hold. When a large share of published results cannot be reproduced, the credibility of an entire field is called into question.

Several factors contribute to this problem. Small sample sizes, flexible analysis procedures, and a bias toward publishing striking results all make false positives more likely. In response, many journals now require pre-registration of hypotheses, which commits authors to a method before data are collected.

questions.text: According to the passage, what do replication studies attempt to do?
options: Repeat earlier experiments to check whether the original findings hold
Replace older theories with new ones
Publish only results that are striking
Reduce the number of participants in experiments

questions.text: According to the passage, what do many journals now require?
options: The removal of all statistical analysis

questions.text: What can be inferred about the bias toward publishing striking results?
options: It may encourage researchers to report findings that are less reliable
It guarantees that replication studies will always succeed
It has no effect on the credibility of a field
It was introduced by editors to reduce publishing costs

questions.text: Why might pre-registration help reduce false positives?
options: It prevents researchers from changing their methods after seeing the data
It makes sample sizes larger automatically
It removes the need for statistical analysis
It allows authors to publish without peer review

vocabulary.definition: the act of repeating a study to check whether its results can be obtained again
the quality of being believable and trustworthy
proposed explanations that are tested through research
a tendency to favour one result or view over others unfairly

paragraph_translations: Tekrar çalışmaları deneysel psikolojide giderek merkezi bir konu haline geldi. Araştırmacılar, orijinal bulguların geçerli olup olmadığını belirlemek için önceki deneyleri aynı yöntemlerle tekrarlamaya çalışıyor. Yayımlanan sonuçların büyük bir kısmı yeniden üretilemediğinde, tüm bir alanın güvenilirliği sorgulanmaya başlanır.

Bu sorunun birkaç nedeni var. Küçük örneklem büyüklükleri, esnek analiz prosedürleri ve çarpıcı sonuçları yayımlama eğilimi, yanlış pozitifleri daha olası kılıyor. Buna karşılık pek çok dergi artık veri toplanmadan önce hipotezlerin önceden kaydedilmesini şart koşuyor; bu da yazarları veri toplanmadan önce bir yönteme bağlıyor.
